points.description: Focal length in pixels: fx = f / pixel width = 16 mm / 0.005 mm = 3200 pixels (fy = fx as pixels are square). Method (f divided by pixel size, with consistent units) and value both needed.

levels.says: Correct method fx = f/pixel size shown but arithmetic or unit-conversion error (e.g. 320 or 32000), or correct value 3200 with no method shown at all.

points.description: Field of view width on the belt = 160 mm, e.g. sensor width 6.4 mm x 400/16 = 160 mm, or 1280 x (400/3200). Accept a value derived from a consistent earlier error only if the method is correct (then no mark for the numeric value unless 160).
Distance on belt per pixel = 0.125 mm (160 mm / 1280, or Z/fx = 400/3200). Either route accepted. Follow-through marks allowed if 160 mm was wrong but divided correctly by 1280.

rubric.notes: Full marks: fx = 3200 px, FOV = 160 mm, 0.125 mm/pixel; either route to (ii) is acceptable. Part marks only for P1 when the method is right but the arithmetic is wrong. Follow-through is allowed for P3 if the division is correct from a wrong FOV.
rubric.answer_key:
(i) fx = f/pixel width = 16 mm / 0.005 mm = 3200 pixels (fy = 3200 too).
(ii) Sensor width = 1280 x 5 µm = 6.4 mm. FOV = 6.4 x 400/16 = 160 mm. One pixel = 160/1280 = 0.125 mm on the belt. (Alternative: dX = Z/fx = 400/3200 = 0.125 mm; FOV = 1280 x 0.125 = 160 mm.)
